title: Good cellular trees for a weakly saturated class
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal U$; small means $\mathcal U$-small, and colimits mean [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. A cardinal $\tau$ is regular if unions of fewer than $\tau$ sets of size less than $\tau$ have size less than $\tau$. A category is $\tau$-filtered if each diagram with fewer than $\tau$ morphisms admits a cocone. An object is $\tau$-presentable if its Hom functor preserves small $\tau$-filtered colimits. Let $\tau\in\mathcal U$ be uncountable regular and let $\mathcal A$ have small Hom sets, all small colimits, and a small family of $\tau$-presentable objects under whose small $\tau$-filtered colimits every object is obtained. A weakly saturated arrow class contains all isomorphisms and is closed under pushouts, small continuous transfinite compositions, and retracts in the arrow category (arrows are objects, commuting squares are morphisms; a retract of $g$ is an $f$ with maps $s:f\to g$, $r:g\to f$ and $rs=1_f$). A pushout is a colimit of a span. Continuous means that at each nonzero limit ordinal the object is the colimit of its predecessors. Let $C$ be weakly saturated, and let $K$ be the class of its arrows with $\tau$-presentable source and target. Suppose $C$ is the weakly saturated closure of a small subset of $K$.

For any arrow class $L$, an $L$-tree with root $X$ consists of a small well-founded poset $T$ (each nonempty subset has a minimal element), a diagram $t\mapsto(X\to Y_t)$ in the undercategory $X/\mathcal A$ (its objects are maps out of $X$, and its morphisms are commuting triangles), and, for every $t$, a map $P_t\to Q_t$ in $L$ and an attaching map $P_t\to Y_{<t}$ such that the canonical map $Y_{<t}\to Y_t$ induced by the diagram is a pushout of $P_t\to Q_t$ along the attaching map: there is a map $Q_t\to Y_t$ making the square commute, and the square is a pushout, so $Y_t\cong Y_{<t}\amalg_{P_t}Q_t$ by an isomorphism under $Y_{<t}$. Here $Y_{<t}$ is the colimit of the predecessor diagram in $X/\mathcal A$; an empty colimit in that undercategory is $X$. For downward-closed $E\subseteq T$ write $Y_E$ for the restricted colimit in $X/\mathcal A$, so $Y_\varnothing=X$. Such a tree is $\tau$-good if $P_t,Q_t$ are $\tau$-presentable and each predecessor set has cardinality less than $\tau$.

Every $f:X\to Y$ in $C$ admits a $\tau$-good $K$-tree with $X\to Y_T$ isomorphic to $f$ in $X/\mathcal A$. For every $L$-tree and downward-closed $E\subseteq F\subseteq T$, the map $Y_E\to Y_F$ belongs to the weakly saturated closure of $L$. If the tree is $\tau$-good, this map is itself the colimit map of a $\tau$-good $L$-tree with root $Y_E$ and indexing poset $F\setminus E$, with the inherited order.
